items.mnemonic: A SMALL badge pinned beneath a COVER of banners, and a forest of LEGS marching under it in step — the loyal members of a political PARTY.
TEN villagers add their POWER, POWER and POWER to one rope and the boulder finally rolls off the road — many arms heaving together is how you COOPERATE.
One THREAD is split EIGHT ways and tied to the PRIVATE HEART of every villager, then drawn tight so all of them are gathered into one WHOLE.
A PERSON raises ONE banner tipped with a carved bird BEAK and plants it at the HEAD of the valley, claiming every field below as TERRITORY.
The foreman stands in the mud to SAY where each post will go, and a pike-like WEAPON is driven in as a marker — that is how you ESTABLISH a camp.
A coiled SNAKE of old habits gets one sharp STRIKE from the master's stick and straightens out on the spot — a REFORM.
Under a LEAN-TO roof one PERSON measures every petition to the INCH before stamping it — the GOVERNMENT OFFICE.
An inspector climbs the TREE outside the window to peer at the top SHELF where the hidden ledgers sit — nothing escapes her when she sets out to INVESTIGATE.
A farmer piles his whole harvest of GRAIN at the feet of a WOMAN with a steady ledger and walks away without counting — he can ENTRUST it to her.
A COVER of canvas is thrown over every war CAR so the enemy cannot count the wheels — the camp of an ARMY on the move.
Inside a square ENCLOSURE the members stand an INCH apart, shoulder to shoulder, so tightly packed that they move as one GROUP.
A raw hide is pegged flat on a frame, scraped and worked until the skin is transformed into something smooth and tough — LEATHER.
A boulder of EARTH splits EIGHT ways and every ROUND lump goes bounding downhill, gaining POWER with each turn — unstoppable FORCE.
WATER drips from the tip of a HALBERD into ONE open MOUTH; every drop swallowed is one less in the bucket, and the level starts to DECREASE.
ONE beam laid across the FRAME, EARTH packed in, then the whole wall knocked down and built a second time — AGAIN.
The collector scoops a share of GRAIN, blows the HORNS, opens his MOUTH to announce the sum and hurries off on quick LEGS — that is the TAX.
Under a SMALL lantern and a COVER of canvas, one MOUTH takes orders while another MOUTH calls them back to the stove — this is how you MANAGE a night stall.
Two people stand side by side, each sneaking a glance at the other's height — the very picture of COMPARE.
A guard on the HILL turns to face each DIRECTION in turn; whatever flood or foe approaches, he is already there to PREVENT it.
Torn CLOTHES are mended with a patch cut square as a SEEDBED, filling the hole so neatly you cannot tell — a SUPPLEMENT for what was missing.
A ridge of EARTH marks where one village's SOUND of bells fades and another's begins; a pair of LEGS crosses it in a single stride — the BOUNDARY.
Down a dark ROAD a guide carries a lantern at NECK height, staying exactly an INCH ahead of the travelers so they never lose him — that is how you GUIDE.
A full WINE JUG stands beside the master's chair while his second-in-command waits one step behind with a SWORD: not the chief himself, but his trusted DEPUTY.
BAMBOO counting rods are laid out under one careful EYE while TWO HANDS slide them back and forth — the ancient way to CALCULATE.
The CAR rolls out at dawn: a PERSON drives, ONE last MOON hangs in the sky, and a SWORD guards the crates on the long haul — TRANSPORT.
On the ROAD a witness points at the TREE and the single DROP of red paint beneath it, telling exactly what she saw — each detail she can MENTION.
A THREAD trails from a bubbling SPRING, pulled straight and long across the field until it is one unbroken LINE.
A farmer bends in a CURVE over the furrow, scraping the soil with a sharp SCALLOP shell for a hoe — the oldest tool of AGRICULTURE.
A RIVER runs in three channels, and in each one a DROP of dry land rises; settlers build on those sandbanks until the river land is a STATE.
A HALBERD planted upright where the marching feet STOP: the warrior's weapon at rest is the emblem of the MILITARY.
Its trunk BOUND UP in a curl above a wide MOUTH, a grey beast far bigger than any PIG lumbers past the gate — the ELEPHANT.
A plot of EARTH guarded by a HALBERD, with a MOUTH to challenge strangers and ONE line scratched all the way around — a REGION with its own border.
A guest under the ROOF arrives on WALKING LEGS with his MOUTH open for dinner, then is handed a bill so steep that his HEAD rocks back — look at that AMOUNT.
A sailor opens a BOX marked with a CROSS, finds maps of cathedrals and canals inside, and stretches into a long YAWN after the voyage — EUROPE.
A HAND hoists the SUN onto ONE shoulder like a sack of rice and sets off down the road — a heavy load to CARRY.
A level of still WATER with a SMALL BIRD floating on it and TEN marks scratched along the side; against this the surveyor measures everything — the STANDARD.
A SMALL crown sits above a FRAME; a MOUTH reads out the winner's name and a SHELL of old money is pressed into her palm — the PRIZE.
Beside the ROAD a SWORD is thrust into the ground as a marker: everything within a stone's throw of it counts as the VICINITY.
Down the ROAD plods a COW, MOUTH full of straw, timber strapped to its back; at the site the carpenters unload it and start to MAKE.
CLOTHES pulled over bare SKIN against a storm nobody asked for — whoever wears them is the one who has to SUFFER.
One HAND repeats the same motion TEN thousand times until the RIGHT HAND can do it blindfolded — that is SKILL.
A PERSON bows before the CLAN banner until his back is ONE flat line with the floor — as LOW as a body can go.
A STEP out the door, a PERSON walking under the SUN all day, and the same WALKING LEGS carrying him back along the same path at dusk, until everything is as it was — RESTORE.
A stalk of GRAIN is dug up one EVENING and planted in a new field the next EVENING — from plot to plot, a slow MOVE.
One PERSON steps into an ENCLOSURE built of TEN planks with a single MOUTH-shaped window, alone in a box of his own — one INDIVIDUAL.
Two tall doors swinging on their hinges, wide enough for a cart to pass between them — the temple's GATE.
The chief stands to SAY which FRUIT of this quarter's work each desk must deliver — the duties of one SECTION.
Inside the MOON-pale skull two HORNS of nerve rise from a CONTAINER where thoughts CROSS and tangle in every direction — the BRAIN.
A TREE on ONE last ridge, a HOOK hanging from its branch, a MOUTH shouting into the wind and a RIGHT HAND clamped to the bark: this is the farthest anyone has climbed, the EXTREME.
Right NOW the MOUTH holds a sweet without chewing or swallowing, keeping it safely inside — INCLUDE.
Under a thatch of GRASS a BED is pushed against the wall, a HALBERD leans beside it, and a RETAINER sleeps across the doorway to guard the treasure — the STOREHOUSE.
From SUN-up, ONE clerk walks the VILLAGE with a scale, weighing every sack of rice until he knows the whole QUANTITY.
ONE block of clay, TWO HANDS pressing it flat, a SWORD trimming the edges, EARTH baked hard around the shape so a hundred copies can be cast — the MODEL.
WATER up to the LEGS, and a big brother cupping his MOUTH to shout a report across the flood on the present CONDITION.
A sliver of GOLD metal filed thin, with a TEN-shaped cross of pins beside it, sharp enough to slip through silk — a NEEDLE.
TEN years spent on a single RICE FIELD, knowing every INCH of its soil and nothing else — the devotion of a SPECIALTY.
A scribe sets his brush in the MIDDLE of the page and pulls one long STROKE down through the years — recording HISTORY.
Steps climb the HILL; at every landing you COMPARE the view with the one below, until the WHITE top step is reached; each landing is one FLOOR.
A length of BAMBOO runs under the ROOF and across a HEAP of earth, carrying water from the well into the kitchen — a PIPE.
An AXE gripped by ONE man standing with his feet spread like EIGHT, ready at the gate — a SOLDIER.
A HAND reaches out to a WOMAN who has taken her STAND at the doorway; the moment their palms meet is CONTACT.
A single THREAD stretched across a RICE FIELD, so slender you lose it against the sky — THIN.
Lift the LID of the medicine pot, let FATHER drink, and watch the POWER return to his arms within the hour — that is the EFFECT.
A nine with a drop tucked inside it rolls across the table like a pill: perfectly ROUND.
WATER curls inland under a LID of fog, spreading EIGHT ways before the shore bends it back like a drawn BOW — a BAY.
A GOLD plate is swept clean with a BROOM, rinsed with WATER and engraved line by line so the deed can never be lost — a RECORD.
Narrow the SMALL gap between the lids to a single STROKE; the EYE shuts out the clutter and turns inward to REFLECT.
A single STROKE stands beside the SUN like a tally mark for every day already gone: the former, the OLD.
A TREE trunk is laid across the gorge; a YOUTH climbs onto it, builds a FRAME above the water and leaves a MOUTH-sized gap for boats to pass under — a BRIDGE.
A MOUNTAIN drops to a CLIFF, and at its foot a CLOTHESLINE of fishing nets is strung where land meets water — the SHORE.
Inside a FRAME of walls lies a plot of EARTH with a MOUTH-shaped well; walk the wall once around and you have traced the CIRCUMFERENCE.
A carpenter walks the forest tapping each TREE, listening for the one with TALENT in its grain — the perfect MATERIAL.
A BIG figure stands inside a FRAME with arms touching both sides, hanging exactly in the CENTER.
Blow the HORNS, and the HUSBAND at the counter cuts the paper slip in two with a SWORD so the stub can be matched later — a TICKET.
A THREAD passes behind the DOOR and through the bamboo slips of a BOOKSHELF, binding loose pages into one volume — COMPILE.
One HAND holds a torch bright as LIGHTNING while the RIGHT HAND feels along the dark floor for the lost key — SEARCH.
RUN past the guard with his SWORD and the herald with his MOUTH wide open, straight over the finish line and beyond it — EXCEED.
Two figures standing shoulder to shoulder with their feet planted on one line: a ROW.
Under the SICKNESS roof lies a BIG patient; nurses open the shutters to let the SUN pour over him and spoon in SMALL sips of broth until he is well — HEAL.
A HAND reaches up like a CLAW into the TREE and plucks the ripest fruit from the branch — PICK.
Two brothers STAND side by side, each MOUTH shouting louder than the other, LEGS tensed for the whistle — COMPETE.
A person squeezed between two posts like a WEDGE, holding the gap open so the two sides can reach each other — MEDIATE.
A TREE as STUBBORN as a mule refuses to be pulled up, because it has anchored itself deep in the earth with its ROOT.
A merchant takes SHELL money at the foot of a CLIFF and hands over the goods with his RIGHT HAND as fast as he can count — SELL.
Under a CLIFF stand two rows of TREE trunks carved with dates; the traveler must STOP at each one and read how far he has come — HISTORY.
Beside his camp BED in the EVENING the officer studies the map an INCH at a time, planning tomorrow's march — the COMMANDER.
A bolt of CLOTH is unrolled until it is as wide as a fat WINE JUG is round — measure that and you have its WIDTH.
A flat BOAT poles across the river with a WEAPON lying in the bottom, carrying folk of every kind — the ordinary run of things, GENERAL.
